![](../assets/thumbs/ch12.png){width=60% fig-align=center fig-alt="Quantum reservoir computing"}

In quantum reservoir computing the many-body dynamics itself is left untrained: an input sequence is written into
a spin system, the Hamiltonian evolution acts as a nonlinear feature map with fading memory, and only a linear
readout is fitted by ridge regression. The notebook measures the memory capacity of the reservoir, applies it to
standard benchmark tasks, and compares density-tensor and trajectory simulations under finite measurement
statistics and decoherence.

## Notebooks in this chapter

::: {.nb-item}
[Quantum reservoir computing — many-body dynamics as a machine for time series](../ch12_quantum_reservoir_computing/46_quantum_reservoir_computing.ipynb)

A driven many-body spin system as a trainable machine: input injection by qubit reset (a replacement channel), Hamiltonian dynamics between injections as a feature map with fading memory, ridge-regression readout, memory capacity and its finite-data bias, NARMA and Santa Fe laser prediction against tuned classical baselines, density tensor versus trajectories, finite measurement statistics and decoherence.
:::
